paragraphs.text: On that day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
paragraphs.translit: En tē hēmera ekeinē exelthōn ho Iēsous tēs oikias ekathēto para tēn thalassan·

paragraphs.text: And there were gathered unto him great multitudes, so that he entered into a boat, and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.
paragraphs.original: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
paragraphs.translit: kai synēchthēsan pros auton ochloi polloi, hōste auton eis ploion embanta kathēsthai, kai pas ho ochlos epi ton aigialon heistēkei.

paragraphs.text: And he spake to them many things in parables, saying, Behold, the sower went forth to sow;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elalēsen autois polla en parabolais legōn· Idou exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirein.

paragraphs.text: and as he sowed, some [seeds] fell by the way side, and the birds came and devoured them:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tō speirein auton ha men epesen para tēn hodon, kai elthonta ta peteina katephagen auta.

paragraphs.text: and others fell upon the rocky places, where they had not much earth: and straightway they sprang up, because they had no deepness of earth:
paragraphs.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς,
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi ta petrōdē hopou ouk eichen gēn pollēn, kai eutheōs exaneteilen dia to mē echein bathos gēs,

paragraphs.text: and when the sun was risen, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.
paragraphs.original: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
paragraphs.translit: hēliou de anateilantos ekaumatisthē kai dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē.

paragraphs.text: And others fell upon the thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked them:
paragraphs.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἔπνιξαν αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi tas akanthas, kai anebēsan hai akanthai kai epnixan auta.

paragraphs.text: and others fell upon the good ground, and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn kai edidou karpon, ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.

paragraphs.text: He that hath ears, let him hear.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: ho echōn ōta akouetō.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
paragraphs.translit: Kai proselthontes hoi mathētai eipan autō· Dia ti en parabolais laleis autois;

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτι ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Hoti hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn, ekeinois de ou dedotai.

paragraphs.text: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hostis gar echei, dothēsetai autō kai perisseuthēsetai· hostis de ouk echei, kai ho echei arthēsetai apʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: Therefore speak I to them in parables; because seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto en parabolais autois lalō, hoti blepontes ou blepousin kai akouontes ouk akouousin oude syniousin·

paragraphs.text: And unto them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no wise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no wise perceive:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
paragraphs.translit: kai anaplēroutai autois hē prophēteia Ēsaiou hē legousa· Akoē akousete kai ou mē synēte, kai blepontes blepsete kai ou mē idēte.

paragraphs.text: For this people`s heart is waxed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
paragraphs.original: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: epachynthē gar hē kardia tou laou toutou, kai tois ōsin bareōs ēkousan, kai tous ophthalmous autōn ekammysan· mēpote idōsin tois ophthalmois kai tois ōsin akousōsin kai tē kardia synōsin kai epistrepsōsin, kai iasomai autous.

paragraphs.text: But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
paragraphs.original: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hymōn de makarioi hoi ophthalmoi hoti blepousin, kai ta ōta hymōn hoti akouousin.

paragraphs.text: For verily I say unto you, that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which ye see, and saw them not; and to hear the things which ye hear, and heard them not.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
paragraphs.translit: amēn gar legō hymin hoti polloi prophētai kai dikaioi epethymēsan idein ha blepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai ha akouete kai ouk ēkousan.

paragraphs.text: Hear then ye the parable of the sower.
paragraphs.original: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis oun akousate tēn parabolēn tou speirantos.

paragraphs.text: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, [then] cometh the evil [one], and snatcheth away that which hath been sown in his heart. This is he that was sown by the way side.
paragraphs.original: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
paragraphs.translit: pantos akouontos ton logon tēs basileias kai mē synientos, erchetai ho ponēros kai harpazei to esparmenon en tē kardia autou· houtos estin ho para tēn hodon spareis.

paragraphs.text: And he that was sown upon the rocky places, this is he that heareth the word, and straightway with joy receiveth it;
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: ho de epi ta petrōdē spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai euthys meta charas lambanōn auton,

paragraphs.text: yet hath he not root in himself, but endureth for a while; and when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, straightway he stumbleth.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
paragraphs.translit: ouk echei de rhizan en heautō alla proskairos estin, genomenēs de thlipseōs ē diōgmou dia ton logon euthys skandalizetai.

paragraphs.text: And he that was sown among the thorns, this is he that heareth the word; and the care of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eis tas akanthas spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn, kai hē merimna tou aiōnos toutou kai hē apatē tou ploutou sympnigei ton logon, kai akarpos ginetai.

paragraphs.text: And he that was sown upon the good ground, this is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; who verily beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de epi tēn kalēn gēn spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai synieis, hos dē karpophorei kai poiei ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.

paragraphs.text: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man that sowed good seed in his field:
paragraphs.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō speiranti kalon sperma en tō agrō autou.

paragraphs.text: but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares also among the wheat, and went away.
paragraphs.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: en de tō katheudein tous anthrōpous ēlthen autou ho echthros kai epespeiren zizania ana meson tou sitou kai apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: But when the blade sprang up and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
paragraphs.translit: hote de eblastēsen ho chortos kai karpon epoiēsen, tote ephanē kai ta zizania.

paragraphs.text: And the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field? whence then hath it tares?
paragraphs.original: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
paragraphs.translit: proselthontes de hoi douloi tou oikodespotou eipon autō· Kyrie, ouchi kalon sperma espeiras en tō sō agrō; pothen oun echei zizania;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, An enemy hath done this. And the servants say unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē autois· Echthros anthrōpos touto epoiēsen. hoi de douloi autō legousin· Theleis oun apelthontes syllexōmen auta;

paragraphs.text: But he saith, Nay; lest haply while ye gather up the tares, ye root up the wheat with them.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
paragraphs.translit: ho de phēsin· Ou, mēpote syllegontes ta zizania ekrizōsēte hama autois ton siton·

paragraphs.text: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather up first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.
paragraphs.original: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
paragraphs.translit: aphete synauxanesthai amphotera mechri tou therismou· kai en kairō tou therismou erō tois theristais· Syllexate prōton ta zizania kai dēsate auta eis desmas pros to katakausai auta, ton de siton synagagete eis tēn apothēkēn mou.

paragraphs.text: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
paragraphs.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn kokkō sinapeōs, hon labōn anthrōpos espeiren en tō agrō autou·

paragraphs.text: which indeed is less than all seeds; but when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and lodge in the branches thereof.
paragraphs.original: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho mikroteron men estin pantōn tōn spermatōn, hotan de auxēthē meizon tōn lachanōn estin kai ginetai dendron, hōste elthein ta peteina tou ouranou kai kataskēnoun en tois kladois autou.

paragraphs.text: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.
paragraphs.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn elalēsen autois· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn zymē, hēn labousa gynē enekrypsen eis aleurou sata tria heōs hou ezymōthē holon.

paragraphs.text: All these things spake Jesus in parables unto the multitudes; and without a parable spake he nothing unto them:
paragraphs.original: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Tauta panta elalēsen ho Iēsous en parabolais tois ochlois, kai chōris parabolēs ouden elalei autois·

paragraphs.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.
paragraphs.original: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs plērōthē to rhēthen dia tou prophētou legontos· Anoixō en parabolais to stoma mou, ereuxomai kekrymmena apo katabolēs.

paragraphs.text: Then he left the multitudes, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Explain unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
paragraphs.original: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Tote apheis tous ochlous ēlthen eis tēn oikian. kai prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai autou legontes· Diasaphēson hēmin tēn parabolēn tōn zizaniōn tou agrou.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ho speirōn to kalon sperma estin ho hyios tou anthrōpou·

paragraphs.text: and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the tares are the sons of the evil [one];
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho de agros estin ho kosmos· to de kalon sperma, houtoi eisin hoi hyioi tēs basileias· ta de zizania eisin hoi hyioi tou ponērou,

paragraphs.text: and the enemy that sowed them is the devil: and the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are angels.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de echthros ho speiras auta estin ho diabolos· ho de therismos synteleia aiōnos estin, hoi de theristai angeloi eisin.

paragraphs.text: As therefore the tares are gathered up and burned with fire; so shall it be in the end of the world.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ καίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος·
paragraphs.translit: hōsper oun syllegetai ta zizania kai pyri kaietai, houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos·

paragraphs.text: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and them that do iniquity,
paragraphs.original: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,
paragraphs.translit: apostelei ho hyios tou anthrōpou tous angelous autou, kai syllexousin ek tēs basileias autou panta ta skandala kai tous poiountas tēn anomian,

paragraphs.text: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou pyros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

paragraphs.text: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He that hath ears, let him hear.
paragraphs.original: Τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: Tote hoi dikaioi eklampsousin hōs ho hēlios en tē basileia tou patros autōn. ho echōn ōta akouetō.

paragraphs.text: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in the field; which a man found, and hid; and in his joy he goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.
paragraphs.original: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
paragraphs.translit: Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn thēsaurō kekrymmenō en tō agrō, hon heurōn anthrōpos ekrypsen, kai apo tēs charas autou hypagei kai pōlei panta hosa echei kai agorazei ton agron ekeinon.

paragraphs.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a merchant seeking goodly pearls:
paragraphs.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
paragraphs.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō emporō zētounti kalous margaritas·

paragraphs.text: and having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
paragraphs.original: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: heurōn de hena polytimon margaritēn apelthōn pepraken panta hosa eichen kai ēgorasen auton.

paragraphs.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:
paragraphs.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn sagēnē blētheisē eis tēn thalassan kai ek pantos genous synagagousē·

paragraphs.text: which, when it was filled, they drew up on the beach; and they sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but the bad they cast away.
paragraphs.original: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
paragraphs.translit: hēn hote eplērōthē anabibasantes epi ton aigialon kai kathisantes synelexan ta kala eis angē, ta de sapra exō ebalon.

paragraphs.text: So shall it be in the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the righteous,
paragraphs.original: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
paragraphs.translit: houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos· exeleusontai hoi angeloi kai aphoriousin tous ponērous ek mesou tōn dikaiōn

paragraphs.text: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou pyros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

paragraphs.text: Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea.
paragraphs.original: Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί.
paragraphs.translit: Synēkate tauta panta; legousin autō· Nai.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Therefore every scribe who hath been made a disciple to the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a householder, who bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Dia touto pas grammateus mathēteutheis tē basileia tōn ouranōn homoios estin anthrōpō oikodespotē hostis ekballei ek tou thēsaurou autou kaina kai palaia.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tas parabolas tautas, metēren ekeithen.

paragraphs.text: And coming into his own country he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn eis tēn patrida autou edidasken autous en tē synagōgē autōn, hōste ekplēssesthai autous kai legein· Pothen toutō hē sophia hautē kai hai dynameis;

paragraphs.text: Is not this the carpenter`s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
paragraphs.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
paragraphs.translit: ouch houtos estin ho tou tektonos hyios; ouch hē mētēr autou legetai Mariam kai hoi adelphoi autou Iakōbos kai Iōsēph kai Simōn kai Ioudas;

paragraphs.text: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?
paragraphs.original: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
paragraphs.translit: kai hai adelphai autou ouchi pasai pros hēmas eisin; pothen oun toutō tauta panta;

paragraphs.text: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and in his own house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eskandalizonto en autō. ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi kai en tē oikia autou.

paragraphs.text: And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk epoiēsen ekei dynameis pollas dia tēn apistian autōn.
